messages:
maria: Quick heads-up: I'm revamping the function-invoke docs to be SDK-first and bake in a clear structured-output schema. Goal: fewer ad-hoc curl examples, canonical Python/JS SDK snippets, a strict minimal JSONSchema + a permissive full example, and a short migration note for consumers. Will open PR later today. :clipboard:
aj (sdk): Nice. Include both streaming and non-streaming examples. Also add a tiny helper showing how to do lenient vs strict parsing (one-liner import).
maria: yes. plan = produce: 1) minimal example (fields apps should rely on), 2) full envelope example (metadata + telemetry), 3) streaming snippet. I'll keep old curl examples commented.
samir (eng-ml): Please ensure schema samples match the runtime envelope. we recently added envelope.schema_version and metrics.request_latency_ms — examples without them cause QA drift. Also show array-of-objects outputs for functions that return lists.
maria: good call. minimal schema will be: {"type":"object","properties":{"payload":{"type":"object"}},"required":["payload"]} and full example will show metadata: {"request_id","schema_version","metrics"}.
kai (devex): I can run the anchor-scan after the PR lands. Drop the known-broken anchors in the PR description so my script can target them. I'll also prepare an automated snippet conversion so we don't hand-edit 8 pages.
eva (qa): add a tiny docs-e2e test that parses the sample response with the parser lib. current parser rejects unknownProps=false; we need to allow metadata in full examples or flag as 'example-only' in the schema. I can add the test tomorrow.
aj (sdk): snippet idea for JS (lenient parse):```js
import {Client, parseStructured} from '@redwood/inference'
const client = new Client()
const r = await client.invoke({model: 'rw-invoke-1', function_name: 'get_user_profile', input: 'id:1234'})
// lenient parse allows extra meta fields
const parsed = parseStructured(r, {allowUnknownProps: true})
console.log(parsed.payload)
```
maria: python non-streaming example for docs:```py
from redwood import Client
from redwood.parsers import parse_structured
c = Client()
resp = c.invoke(model='rw-invoke-1', function_name='get_user_profile', input='id:1234')
# strict parse (validate against minimal schema)
obj = parse_structured(resp, strict=True)
print(obj['payload'])
```
docs-bot: link-check queued for PR 975  running anchor scan.
samir (eng-ml): one more: call out that some functions return arrays: show an example where payload = [{"id":1},{"id":2}] and recommend clients use map/reduce patterns not single-object assumptions. mention nullable items in arrays.
maria: will add array example + migration note. big question: rename envelope fields from "kind/body" to "type/payload"? it simplifies docs but is a breaking change.
aj (sdk): i'm fine as long as SDK accepts old names for one release via a compat layer. i'll follow up with a tiny shim PR. not blocking docs PR.
kai (devex): when you update snippets leave commented curl blocks so older examples can be removed in follow-up. reduces churn in release notes.
eva (qa): ETA for test: tomorrow morning. can we gate merge on docs-e2e?
maria: yes  adding docs-e2e as required check in PR. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/975 (WIP). reviewers: @aj, @kai, @samir. aiming EOW for review, merge early next week after docs-e2e/link-check pass. ping here if blocked. :rocket:
